sentences.text: 2. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

(Add) 
3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant oppose the bail application and submit that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.

4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant and perused the challan papers particularly, the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the content of the FIR which got lodged at the behest of the father of the victim.
5.

The FIR which came to be lodged on 14.05.2023 by the father of the victim for the incident which took place on 11.05.2023, however, no explanation has been furnished with regard to the delay occasioned in filing of the FIR.
The submission at the behest of the accused seems to be worth considering that the possibility of embellishment and concoction cannot be ruled out.
The father of the victim alleged in the FIR that the incident took place on 11.05.2023 at around 9.00 P.M. at his home when his daughter was molested.

However, when the girl was examined under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. on 15.05.2023, she alleged that on [2023:RJ-JD:30556] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-10910/2023]
11.05.2023, when her parents were not at home, the accused entered into her house forcibly and pelted stone, however, no incident of subjecting her to rape was mentioned therein except the bald accusation that on previous two occasions, she was subjected to rape.
When she was examined under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate on 16.05.2023, a serious incongruence with regard to the manner of incident can be observed.
After investigation, a charge sheet has been filed.
Another FIR No.222/2023 lodged at the behest of the sister of the petitioner further corroborating the submission made by the petitioner regarding false allegation

. 
Considering the overall submissions while refraining from passing any comments on the niceties of the matter as the same may put an adverse effect on the merits of the case, yet considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as the fact that there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
Needless to say, none of the observations made herein under shall affect the rights of either of the parties during trial and this Court refrains from commenting on the niceties of the matter.

6. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the [2023:RJ-JD:30556] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-10910/2023] learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
